solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boy back in hospital, brought with feet strapped?

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital for convalescents

indicators.note: back says the word for the boy is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: a lad is a boy
led means brought, as in led someone along

explanation.surface: A young lad, back in hospital, is wheeled in with his feet bandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with feet strapped?' looks like an injury to go with the hospital, but it describes someone in open shoes held on by straps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing sandals has footwear held on by straps, hence the question mark on this playful description.

clue.text: Old US scientist bags ore for breaking down

indicators.note: ore being broken down for processing suggests the letters are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist pockets some ore to break down in the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Seaborg was a twentieth-century American chemist who discovered plutonium and other heavy elements.

clue.text: Fool's purse picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard or caught by ear, so we take a word as spoken

parts.note: to purse the brows is to knit them together

explanation.surface: A fool lets someone pick up his purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purse' looks like a noun, a bag that could be picked up; it is the verb, as in knitting the brows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is British slang for a silly, foolish person, short for nitwit.

clue.text: Points in wonderment, wine being served

indicators.note: in places the compass points inside the word for wonderment

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonderment
N and S are the north and south points of the compass
red is wine of that colour

explanation.surface: Someone gapes in wonder as wine is poured out.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a purpose is to serve it, so something that served is something that did the job.

clue.text: One supposedly never free to start releasing article

indicators.note: releasing means letting the article go, so it drops out of the word for start

parts.note: a launch is the start of a venture
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something that is never at liberty begins to let go of an object.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says there is no such thing as a free meal of this sort: everything has a hidden cost.

clue.text: Nothing within poor melodist's range

indicators.note: within places the zero inside the scrambled letters
a poor melodist's notes come out badly ordered, hence the rearrangement

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bad composer has no range at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges MELODIST and 'within' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dolomites are a mountain range in north-eastern Italy.

clue.text: Influential body monarchy legitimately incorporates

indicators.note: incorporates says the letters are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A powerful institution is legally part of the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology, this term names the ruling planet or heavenly body that governs a person's life.

clue.text: Raising family in school, mostly

indicators.note: in puts the relatives inside the shortened school
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: a high school
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Bringing up children in a school, most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiking prices means raising them, a sense of putting up or increasing.

clue.text: Wanting a hand up, being so ineffectual?

definitions.text: Wanting a hand up, being so ineffectual?

parts.words: Wanting a hand up, being so ineffectual?
parts.note: someone whose joint at the hand is too floppy needs help raising it; the phrase also means weak or effete

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue plays on a floppy wrist that cannot hold a hand up, and the phrase's figurative sense of feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes someone limp and ineffectual, with a literally drooping wrist suggesting weakness.

clue.text: Hurry, as guy did, playing piano

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with into a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Hurry up, as that chap did when playing the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: This call to a horse urges it to go faster, so it is a command to hurry.

clue.text: Master is biased, bypassing Head

indicators.note: bypassing the head means skipping the first letter of the word

parts.note: partisan means biased, taking sides

explanation.surface: A teacher is prejudiced and goes over the headmaster's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A master craftsman is a skilled manual worker, a skilled worker in a trade.

clue.text: Wildly fancy idea behind nuclear armament?

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
MAD is mutually assured destruction, the doctrine behind nuclear deterrence

explanation.surface: A wild, fanciful notion underlying the arms race.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something furiously or with great energy, much as wildly does.

clue.text: Job of linesman to secure team compound

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast around, so the poem encloses the team

parts.note: a linesman here is a poet, a writer of lines, and an ode is one of his jobs
XI is eleven, a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A football assistant referee's task is to protect the team's training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' suggests a football official; read it as someone who writes lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical compound of oxygen with another element, such as rust or water.

clue.text: From prayer leader embracing wife, an expression of scorn?

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the wife goes within the prayer leader

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque
'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: Coming from the man leading prayers, a hug for his wife seems a sneering gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' (Dutch = wife) is London slang, from duchess. The 'an' in the definition is also used in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to dismiss a claim scornfully, meaning if that is true then I'm someone else entirely.

clue.text: Writer may whinge if disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author may complain if interrupted while working.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist, author of The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Shell from grenade-launcher behaves like burning ammunition

indicators.note: shell means the outside, so take the first and last letters of the hyphenated word

parts.note: to ape is to imitate, behave like
hot means burning

explanation.surface: A shell from a grenade launcher acts like live ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' looks military but it signals the outer letters G and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Small iron balls fired in a cluster from a cannon, an old form of artillery ammunition.

clue.text: Conned punter ought to

parts.note: to be taken in or duped is to be 'had'
a punter is a gambler, one who bets

explanation.surface: A gambler who was swindled should do something about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses obligation or advisability, as in should, before a verb.

clue.text: Foremost of surfing paradises on Caribbean strand

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the first letters after the islands

parts.note: WI is the West Indies

indicators.note: foremost means the leading letter of each following word

explanation.surface: The best surfing spots line a Caribbean beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strand' suggests a beach to go with surfing; it means a thin thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin strand or thread, as of hair or smoke.

clue.text: Section of motorway tunnel originally cutting through nuclear base

indicators.note: cutting through puts the initial letter inside the base's name

parts.note: Faslane is the Scottish naval base for Britain's nuclear submarines

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A road tunnel being dug beneath a nuclear base.
explanation.walkthrough: FASLANE is the Clyde base of the UK's Trident submarines.
explanation.definitionFit: On a British motorway, the outside lane used for overtaking is a section of the road.

clue.text: Blow a draught

definitions.meaning: a large gulp of drink, especially spirits

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to hit hard and a swig of liquor, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Beanpole, muddy, mostly working out, by the sound of it

indicators.note: mostly means dropping the final letter of the word

parts.note: slimy means muddy and slippery

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for a workout room is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a gym is where you work out

explanation.surface: A tall skinny person, covered in mud after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall, very thin person is called a beanpole, a lanky figure.

clue.text: Strip down from girl's coat

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so DI'S
a mantle is a cloak or coat

explanation.surface: Undressing by taking off a girl's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To take apart a machine or structure piece by piece.

clue.text: Upon which a little corn comes before clay

indicators.note: comes before puts the cereal head first in the answer

parts.note: an ear is a small part, a single head, of corn
then means upon which, next

explanation.surface: A field where a little corn grows before the clay is reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a clay pot: made of baked soil or pottery.

clue.text: Images upsetting I judge, in part

indicators.note: upsetting, in a down clue, turns the whole lot upside down
in puts the letters inside the word for part

parts.note: some means a part of something

explanation.surface: Pictures that I, as a judge, find partly upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and J inside SOME, making SIJOME, and 'upsetting' turns that back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small digital pictures or icons used in text messages.

clue.text: Bearer of one note combined with gift

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
cum is Latin for with, used to mean combined with (a kitchen-cum-diner)
a bent is a natural gift or talent

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a single note together with a present.
explanation.definitionFit: An office-holder bears the office, so the current holder is its bearer.

clue.text: All players having succeeded for the third time in African race

indicators.note: read as S standing for the third T, or time, in the word

parts.note: tutti is a musical direction for all players

explanation.surface: Everyone taking part won at the third attempt in a race in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests a running event; it means a people. T is the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, an ethnic group of central Africa.

clue.text: House having turnover of staff quite regularly

indicators.note: turnover means the combined letters are turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A firm where the employees change fairly often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes U and T from 'quite'; 'turnover of' reverses RODUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house, the English dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Sail through before green and black craft

parts.note: to sail through traffic lights before they turn green is to jump them
jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Speeding through the lights in a green and black car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green and black' look like a colour scheme; 'green' belongs with the lights and 'black' alone gives the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft able to take off vertically, such as the Harrier, is a kind of flying craft.

clue.text: Hateful how satellite cable may be connected!

definitions.text: how satellite cable may be connected!
definitions.meaning: a satellite cable is plugged into a receiving dish, read as three words

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means repulsive and loathsome, from the old view of the creature as hateful.

clue.text: Lyricist whose change of name was provisional?

definitions.text: Lyricist whose change of name was provisional?

parts.words: Lyricist whose change of name was provisional?
parts.note: Gershwin, born Israel, shortened his name to that of the Provisional Irish republican group

explanation.walkthrough: The Provisional Irish Republican Army shares its initials with the first name of George Gershwin's lyricist brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin the lyricist was born Israel Gershowitz, and his chosen first name matches the paramilitary group's initials.

clue.text: Overheard plea to be bombed less

indicators.note: overheard says the words are heard, not seen written

parts.note: mine us is a request to have explosives laid against us

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on a request to be bombed less often.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, take away: subtracting, with the sense of reduced by.

clue.text: Throw a wobbly bucket down, incurring instant fine

indicators.note: incurring means taking on, so the downpour takes in the other letters

parts.note: to bucket down is to rain heavily
sec is short for a second, an instant
A1 means first-rate, fine; the 1 reads as I

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper when it pours and a fine is slapped on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw a wobbly' is British slang for having a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to cause a great commotion or fly into a rage.
